# MISTAKES

> This file records coding mistakes made by LLM agents in this repository.
> Read it before making any code modification so previously identified mistakes are not repeated.
>
> When a new mistake is discovered, add a concise entry that includes:
> - what was done incorrectly
> - why it was incorrect
> - the correct approach to follow next time
>
> Keep entries brief, specific, and actionable. Record repository-specific lessons, not generic advice.

- 2026-08-14 | Treated immediate post-start frontend HTTP probes as definitive after `docker compose up -d` | The frontend container starts only after the API is healthy, so the first host probe can race nginx and return `000` even when the stack is fine | After cold-start validation in this repo, rerun live HTTP checks against the already-running stack before diagnosing a frontend failure
- 2026-08-15 | Renamed the web entry files to `.ts` and `.tsx` without updating `apps/web/tsconfig.json` include globs | The first web type-check passed while skipping the renamed files, which hid the real conversion errors | After any JS→TS rename in this repo, update the workspace `tsconfig.json` include patterns before trusting a type-check result
- 2026-08-15 | Added a Playwright-only rate-limit bypass by reading `process.env` directly in API middleware | This repo forbids direct `process.env` reads outside the validated env loader, and lint correctly rejected the shortcut | When a new runtime flag is needed here, add it to `apps/api/src/config/env.ts` and consume it via `getEnv()` instead of bypassing config validation
- 2026-08-16 | Ran `npm run test` and `npm run test:e2e` in parallel while both workflows manage local DB/server resources | This repo's unit/integration suite and Playwright webServer setup contend for the same MariaDB container and startup window, producing harness failures unrelated to app behavior | In this repo, run the full unit/integration suite, coverage suite, and Playwright suite serially when validating phase gates
- 2026-08-16 | Added DB-backed files to `test:security` without constraining Vitest worker parallelism | The migration and security integration files each recreate the shared MariaDB test database, so parallel workers produced cross-file `Unknown database` and missing-table failures unrelated to the app | In this repo, keep DB-resetting security suites on a single Vitest worker unless each file gets its own isolated database
- 2026-08-16 | Reused the default Docker Compose project name for both the dev stack and `docker-compose.prod.yml` | The production stack and the Playwright/dev stack treated each other as orphaned services and clobbered containers during startup, which broke the prod DB and masked the real failure | In this repo, keep `docker-compose.prod.yml` on its own explicit Compose project name so local prod validation and dev/E2E workflows cannot interfere
- 2026-08-16 | Resolved the migration root from `__dirname` as if source and built layouts were identical | The compiled API runs from `apps/api/dist/src/db`, one directory deeper than source, so the prod migration runner saw zero migrations and left the schema empty | When file paths are used from code that runs in both source and build output here, check both layouts explicitly instead of assuming the same relative depth
- 2026-08-16 | Reused the full API runtime env schema for migration and rollback scripts | Those DB-only entrypoints exited on unrelated web/runtime settings like malformed `CORS_ORIGIN`, which can block first-boot schema setup even though the database settings are correct | In this repo, DB scripts should validate only the DB and logging variables they actually use, with the full API schema reserved for the HTTP runtime
- 2026-08-16 | Trusted Compose service health as sufficient proof that MariaDB was ready for migration traffic on every environment | Slower first-boot environments can report the DB container healthy before remote app-user auth or initial connection readiness is stable, which makes the one-shot migration container fail needlessly | In this repo, the migration runner itself should retry transient DB startup and auth readiness errors instead of relying only on Compose health ordering
- 2026-08-16 | Treated a healthy MariaDB container as proof that the app credentials still matched after changing the TrueNAS compose passwords | MariaDB only applies `MYSQL_USER` and `MYSQL_PASSWORD` when the data directory is first initialized, so a reused bind-mounted data directory can leave `db` healthy while `migrate` and `api` fail with access denied | In this repo's persistent Docker deployments, keep the original DB passwords for an existing data directory or wipe the DB directory before redeploying a fresh install with new credentials
- 2026-08-16 | Considered the mobile horizontal-scroll check complete after covering guest mode and create flow only | Organiser mode adds category and item management controls, so layouts that pass in guest mode can still overflow at phone widths once the extra controls appear alongside max-length names | In this repo, mobile horizontal-scroll regression checks must cover organiser mode with representative max-length content, not just guest mode and create flow
